item.title: Baked Feta Pasta
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: The TikTok-famous baked feta pasta: a whole block of feta roasted with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic and olive oil, mashed into an instant creamy sauce.
item.content:encoded:
Mars here. I resisted this trend for a year, then one lazy Tuesday changed my mind — the oven genuinely does all the work, and the result earns the views.

The TikTok-famous baked feta pasta: a whole block of feta roasted with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic and olive oil, mashed into an instant creamy sauce.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • Roasting concentrates everything: the tomatoes burst and caramelize while the feta softens into a salty cream — flavor you cannot get on a stovetop.
  • Feta is the sauce: its saltiness seasons the entire dish; you barely add anything else.
  • One baking dish: the sauce builds itself in the oven while you do something else entirely.

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket. A few notes on what makes each ingredient work:

  • Feta: buy a block in brine, not crumbles — crumbles are drier and never melt as creamy.
  • Tomatoes: cherry or grape only; large tomatoes water the sauce down.
  • Pasta: ridged shapes like rigatoni grab the chunky sauce best.
  • Use a dish just big enough — tomatoes crowded snugly steam and burst rather than drying out.
  • Mash and mix while everything is hot; the sauce comes together in seconds.
  • The pasta water is not optional here — the sauce needs it to coat instead of clump.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet or nonstick pan
  • Baking sheet or baking dish
  • Large pot for boiling pasta
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Sharp knife and cutting board

Baked Feta Pasta

The TikTok-famous baked feta pasta: a whole block of feta roasted with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic and olive oil, mashed into an instant creamy sauce.

Prep 5 min
Cook 35 min
Total 40 min
Serves 4
Calories 520 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the tomatoes, garlic and most of the olive oil in a baking dish.

  2. 2

    Place the feta block in the center, drizzle with remaining oil, and season everything with chili flakes, oregano and pepper.

  3. 3

    Bake 30-35 minutes until the tomatoes burst and the feta is golden at the edges.

  4. 4

    Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted water; reserve 1 cup pasta water.

  5. 5

    Mash the feta and tomatoes together into a creamy sauce.

  6. 6

    Fold in the hot pasta with a splash of pasta water, then the basil. Taste and season.

Pro Tips for Perfect Baked Feta Pasta

  • Don't overcrowd the pan when searing — work in batches so everything browns instead of steaming.
  • Toss or fold gently — overmixing can break apart delicate ingredients like gnocchi or meatballs.
  • Watch the garlic closely once it hits the pan — it goes from fragrant to bitter in seconds.

Variations to Try

  • Swap the pasta shape: any short pasta works in place of what's listed.
  • Dairy-free: use full-fat coconut cream in place of heavy cream.
  • Add protein: stir in cooked chicken, shrimp, or Italian sausage.

Serving Suggestions

A crisp cucumber salad and grilled chicken round it out. For more tomato-forward comfort, my Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta is the year-round version, and the Spicy Garlic Butter Shrimp makes a stunning topper.

  • A simple Caesar or arugula salad
  • Garlic bread
  • Roasted broccoli or green beans
  • Extra Parmesan at the table

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days.

Freezer

Freezes well in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheat

Reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring in between.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use a different cheese?

Goat cheese melts even creamier; ricotta salata or boursin also work. Classic feta gives the signature salty tang.

My sauce came out watery. Why?

Big tomatoes or an oversized dish. Stick to cherry tomatoes, snug dish, and let it bake the full time so the juices concentrate.

Can I add protein?

Absolutely — fold in shredded rotisserie chicken or seared shrimp at the end, or serve it as a side to grilled meat.

item.title: Crispy Bang Bang Shrimp
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Crispy fried shrimp tossed in the legendary bang bang sauce — creamy, sweet and spicy in every bite. A 25-minute homemade version that beats the restaurant original.
item.content:encoded:
Mars here. The famous appetizer, minus the restaurant bill — crispy shrimp in that creamy-sweet-spicy sauce that disappears faster than anything else I make.

Crispy fried shrimp tossed in the legendary bang bang sauce — creamy, sweet and spicy in every bite. A 25-minute homemade version that beats the restaurant original.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • Cornstarch beats flour: it fries lighter and crispier, and stays crunchy longer under the creamy sauce.
  • Buttermilk soak: a quick soak helps the coating cling and gently seasons the shrimp.
  • Sauce ratio is the secret: two parts mayo to one part sweet chili, sharpened with sriracha — the authentic bang bang balance.

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket. A few notes on what makes each ingredient work:

  • Shrimp: large (21/25) hold their juiciness through frying. Thaw frozen shrimp fully and dry well.
  • Sweet chili sauce: Thai-style bottled sauce is the backbone — find it in the Asian aisle.
  • Sriracha: start with one teaspoon; the sauce should tingle, not burn.
  • Keep the oil at a steady 350°F — too cool makes greasy shrimp, too hot burns the coating before the shrimp cooks.
  • Drain on a rack, never paper towels, to keep the bottoms crisp.
  • Sauce just before serving — dressed shrimp soften within minutes.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet or nonstick pan
  • Tongs
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Sharp knife and cutting board

Crispy Bang Bang Shrimp

Crispy fried shrimp tossed in the legendary bang bang sauce — creamy, sweet and spicy in every bite. A 25-minute homemade version that beats the restaurant original.

Prep 10 min
Cook 15 min
Total 25 min
Serves 4
Calories 450 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Whisk the sauce ingredients together and set aside.

  2. 2

    Soak the shrimp in buttermilk for 5 minutes.

  3. 3

    Season the cornstarch with salt and pepper; dredge each shrimp until fully coated.

  4. 4

    Heat 1/2 inch of oil to 350°F (175°C) in a heavy pan.

  5. 5

    Fry the shrimp in batches, 2 minutes per side, until golden and crisp; drain on a rack.

  6. 6

    Toss the hot shrimp gently in the sauce and garnish. Serve immediately.

Pro Tips for Perfect Crispy Bang Bang Shrimp

  • Don't overcrowd the pan when searing — work in batches so everything browns instead of steaming.
  • Whisk or stir constantly once the sauce starts to thicken so it doesn't scorch on the bottom of the pan.
  • Prep and measure every ingredient before you start cooking — it keeps the process smooth and stress-free.

Variations to Try

  • Oven / air-fryer method: Air fryer works well: spray the dredged shrimp with oil and cook at 400°F for 8-9 minutes, flipping once. Oven-baked loses some crunch.
  • Spice level: Mild-medium as written. The sweet chili dominates; sriracha sets the heat level, so adjust it to taste.
  • Swap the seafood: shrimp, salmon, and white fish are interchangeable in most of these recipes with minor timing adjustments.

Serving Suggestions

Over rice, in lettuce cups, or piled on tacos. If shrimp is your weakness, my Spicy Garlic Butter Shrimp is the 10-minute pan version, and the Creamy Tuscan Shrimp the cozy one.

  • Steamed jasmine or coconut rice
  • A crisp green salad
  • Roasted asparagus or broccoli
  • Crusty bread for the sauce

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 2–3 days.

Freezer

Freezes well in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheat

Reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring in between.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I bake or air-fry instead of frying?

Air fryer works well: spray the dredged shrimp with oil and cook at 400°F for 8-9 minutes, flipping once. Oven-baked loses some crunch.

Is bang bang sauce spicy?

Mild-medium as written. The sweet chili dominates; sriracha sets the heat level, so adjust it to taste.

Can I prep anything ahead?

The sauce keeps a week refrigerated, and you can peel and dry the shrimp a day ahead. Dredge and fry just before serving.

item.title: Better-Than-Takeout Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Silky tender beef and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy savory sauce, made in 20 minutes using the restaurant velveting technique.
item.excerpt:encoded: Silky tender beef and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy savory sauce, made in 20 minutes using the restaurant velveting technique.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: 1 lb (450g) flank steak or sirloin, thinly sliced against the grain 1 tsp baking soda (for velveting) 2 tbsp soy sauce (for marinade) 1 tbsp cornstarch (for marinade) 4 cups broccoli florets (about 1 large head) 3 cloves garlic, minced 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated 3 tbsp vegetable oil, divided 1/4 cup oyster sauce 3 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp brown sugar 1 tsp sesame oil 1/2 cup beef broth or water 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/4 tsp white pepper Sesame seeds and green onions for garnish

Velvet the beef: Toss sliced beef with baking soda. Let sit 15 minutes, then rinse well. Pat dry. Marinate in soy sauce and cornstarch for 5 minutes. Mix sauce: Whisk together oyster sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, beef broth, and cornstarch in a small bowl. Set aside. Blanch broccoli: Cook broccoli in boiling salted water for 90 seconds. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside. Sear beef: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking. Add beef in a single layer. Sear without stirring for 60 seconds, then stir-fry 30 more seconds. Remove to a plate. Cook aromatics: Add remaining oil. Add garlic and ginger. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant. Combine: Add broccoli and beef back to the pan. Pour sauce over everything. Toss and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats everything. Serve immediately over rice.

item.title: Birria-Style Beef Tacos
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Birria-style tacos made weeknight-friendly: beef braised in a rich guajillo-tomato broth, stuffed into crisped tortillas with melty cheese, served with consommé for dipping.
item.content:encoded:
Mars here. The taco that broke the internet, simplified for a home kitchen — tender chili-braised beef, crispy red-stained tortillas, and that dunkable consommé.

Birria-style tacos made weeknight-friendly: beef braised in a rich guajillo-tomato broth, stuffed into crisped tortillas with melty cheese, served with consommé for dipping.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • Dried chiles, real depth: guajillo and ancho give the signature brick-red color and gentle warmth — fruity, not fiery.
  • Chuck shreds like silk: the slow braise melts its collagen into both the meat and the consommé.
  • The fat-dip crisp: dipping tortillas in the seasoned braising fat before griddling is what makes birria tacos look and taste like birria tacos.

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket. A few notes on what makes each ingredient work:

  • Dried chiles: guajillo and ancho are mild and sold in most international aisles. No substitutes capture the color.
  • Beef chuck: short ribs add even more richness; brisket works too. Avoid lean cuts.
  • Cheese: Oaxaca is traditional; low-moisture mozzarella melts nearly identically.
  • Toast the soaked, blended sauce in the pot for 2 minutes before adding broth — it deepens noticeably.
  • Do not rush the braise; the beef is ready when it falls apart at a touch, not before.
  • Strain the consommé before serving — a clean, glossy red broth is half the experience.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet or nonstick pan
  • Tongs
  • Instant-read meat thermometer
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Sharp knife and cutting board

Birria-Style Beef Tacos

Birria-style tacos made weeknight-friendly: beef braised in a rich guajillo-tomato broth, stuffed into crisped tortillas with melty cheese, served with consommé for dipping.

Prep 20 min
Cook 2 hr 30 min
Total 2 hr 50 min
Serves 6
Calories 610 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

6 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.

  2. 2

    Blend the chiles with tomatoes, half the onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, cloves and 1 cup of broth until smooth.

  3. 3

    Season and sear the beef in a heavy pot until browned on all sides.

  4. 4

    Pour in the chile sauce, remaining broth and bay leaves. Simmer covered on low for 2.5 hours (or pressure-cook 50 minutes) until the beef shreds easily.

  5. 5

    Shred the beef; skim the red fat from the broth into a shallow bowl.

  6. 6

    Dip tortillas in the fat, fill with beef and cheese, and crisp in a hot skillet 2 minutes per side.

  7. 7

    Serve with cilantro, onion, lime and cups of the strained consommé for dipping.

Pro Tips for Perfect Birria-Style Beef Tacos

  • Don't overcrowd the pan when searing — work in batches so everything browns instead of steaming.
  • Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil — high heat can cause cream-based sauces to separate.
  • Resist lifting the lid while it cooks — every peek lets out heat and adds extra cooking time.
  • Watch the garlic closely once it hits the pan — it goes from fragrant to bitter in seconds.

Variations to Try

  • Spice level: Mild — guajillo and ancho are about color and depth, not heat. Add a chipotle to the blend if you want fire.
  • Swap the protein: ground turkey or chicken work well in place of beef.
  • Lighter version: use lean ground beef (90/10) and drain any excess fat.

Serving Suggestions

Always with cilantro, diced onion, lime, and hot consommé for dunking. Make it a beef feast with my Smash Burger Tacos on taco night, or go quick with the Korean Ground Beef Bowl midweek.

  • Warm tortillas or flatbread
  • Fluffy white rice
  • A crisp cucumber-tomato salad
  • Pickled onions or a tangy slaw

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

Freezer

Freezes well in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheat

Reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring in between.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this authentic birria?

It is a respectful home-style shortcut. Traditional birria is goat or beef with a more complex chile blend — this captures the spirit in a regular kitchen.

Can I make it in a slow cooker or Instant Pot?

Yes — slow cooker 8 hours on low; Instant Pot 50 minutes high pressure with natural release. Sear and blend first either way.

Are birria tacos spicy?

Mild — guajillo and ancho are about color and depth, not heat. Add a chipotle to the blend if you want fire.

item.title: Cajun Chicken Pasta
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Bold cajun-spiced chicken in a rich, smoky cream sauce tossed with pasta — this cajun chicken pasta is better than any restaurant version.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re craving a pasta dish that delivers bold flavor with minimal effort, this Cajun Chicken Pasta is your answer. Golden-seared chicken breast, tender penne, and cherry tomatoes all come together in a smoky, garlicky cream sauce — and it’s on the table in just 30 minutes.

This Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta is the kind of weeknight dinner that tastes like you spent hours in the kitchen. The secret is Cajun seasoning doing all the heavy lifting — giving the chicken a gorgeous crust and transforming a simple cream sauce into something deeply flavorful. Once you try it, it goes straight into your regular rotation.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • One-pan sauce: The chicken juices left in the skillet after searing build the base of the cream sauce — extra flavor with zero extra effort.
  • Cajun seasoning does double duty: It coats the chicken for a smoky crust AND seasons the sauce, so every bite is perfectly spiced.
  • Ready in 30 minutes: From cold pan to table in half an hour — faster than delivery and infinitely more satisfying.
  • Perfectly balanced heat: Creamy and rich with just enough kick — not overpowering, but unmistakably Cajun.

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket. A few notes on what makes each ingredient work:

  • Chicken breast: Slice thin for faster, more even cooking. Chicken thighs also work great and stay extra juicy.
  • Cajun seasoning: Use your favorite store-bought blend or make your own. If you’re salt-sensitive, choose a low-sodium version and adjust to taste.
  • Heavy cream: This is what makes the sauce luxurious. Half-and-half works in a pinch but the sauce will be thinner.
  • Penne: The tubular shape holds the cream sauce beautifully inside. Rigatoni or rotini are great alternatives.
  • Cherry tomatoes: They burst as they cook, adding fresh acidity that cuts through the richness of the cream. Sun-dried tomatoes are a delicious swap.
  • Don’t overcrowd the pan: Sear chicken in a single layer over high heat. Crowding causes steaming instead of browning — and you want that golden crust.
  • Reserve pasta water: A splash of starchy pasta water loosens the sauce and helps it cling to every piece of penne.
  • Add Parmesan off the heat: Stir in Parmesan after removing from heat to prevent the sauce from breaking. It melts in beautifully.
  • Taste before serving: Cajun blends vary in saltiness. Always taste and adjust at the end — a little extra smoked paprika goes a long way.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet or nonstick pan
  • Tongs
  • Large pot for boiling pasta
  • Instant-read meat thermometer
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Sharp knife and cutting board

Cajun Chicken Pasta

Bold cajun-spiced chicken in a rich, smoky cream sauce tossed with pasta — this cajun chicken pasta is better than any restaurant version.

Prep 10 min
Cook 20 min
Total 30 min
Serves 4
Calories 620 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Cook penne pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, drain.

  2. 2

    Coat chicken with Cajun seasoning. Sear in olive oil 3-4 min per side until cooked. Remove and slice.

  3. 3

    In same pan, sauté garlic 30 sec. Add cherry tomatoes 2 min. Pour in broth, scrape fond. Add cream and paprika. Simmer 3-4 min.

  4. 4

    Stir in Parmesan. Add pasta and toss — use pasta water if too thick. Return chicken, garnish with parsley.

Pro Tips for Perfect Cajun Chicken Pasta

  • Don't overcrowd the pan when searing — work in batches so everything browns instead of steaming.
  • Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil — high heat can cause cream-based sauces to separate.
  • Watch the garlic closely once it hits the pan — it goes from fragrant to bitter in seconds.

Variations to Try

  • Spice level: Absolutely. Start with 1 tablespoon of Cajun seasoning instead of 2, and skip the smoked paprika. You’ll still get all the flavor with a much milder heat level.
  • Make-ahead tip: You can cook and store it for up to 4 days. The sauce thickens as it sits, so add a splash of cream or broth when reheating to bring it back to the right consistency.
  • Swap the protein: shrimp or firm tofu both work well in place of chicken with a shorter cook time.

Serving Suggestions

This pasta is a complete meal on its own, but it pairs beautifully with a few simple sides. Crusty garlic bread is a must for soaking up every last drop of that cream sauce. A crisp green salad with a light lemon vinaigrette balances the richness perfectly. Roasted asparagus or sautéed green beans also make excellent companions — something fresh and bright to contrast the bold, spicy flavors.

  • Steamed rice or cauliflower rice
  • A simple green salad with vinaigrette
  • Roasted or steamed vegetables
  • Crusty bread for the sauce

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days.

Freezer

Cream-based sauces can separate when frozen. This dish is best eaten fresh or refrigerated. If freezing, store up to 2 months and stir well when reheating.

Reheat

Warm gently in a skillet over low heat, adding a splash of cream or broth to loosen the sauce. Avoid the microwave if possible — it can make the sauce break.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make this less spicy?

Absolutely. Start with 1 tablespoon of Cajun seasoning instead of 2, and skip the smoked paprika. You’ll still get all the flavor with a much milder heat level.

Can I use a different pasta shape?

Yes! Rigatoni, rotini, fettuccine, or bow ties all work well. Choose a shape that holds sauce — avoid very thin pasta like angel hair.

Can I make this ahead of time?

You can cook and store it for up to 4 days. The sauce thickens as it sits, so add a splash of cream or broth when reheating to bring it back to the right consistency.

What if I don’t have heavy cream?

Half-and-half is the closest substitute — your sauce will be slightly thinner but still delicious. Coconut cream works surprisingly well and adds a subtle sweetness that plays nicely with the Cajun spices.

item.title: Chicken Penne Pasta
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: This creamy chicken penne pasta recipe is ready in 30 minutes in one skillet — juicy seared chicken and penne in a garlic-parmesan cream sauce the whole family will love.
item.content:encoded:
This chicken penne pasta recipe is the weeknight dinner I make when everyone is hungry and nobody wants to wait: juicy golden chicken bites and al dente penne tossed in a garlic-parmesan cream sauce, all in one skillet in about 30 minutes. No fancy technique, no obscure ingredients — just the kind of creamy chicken and penne pasta that gets quiet-table approval every single time.

This chicken penne pasta recipe uses Italian-American flavors and comes together with everyday ingredients — no special trip to a specialty store required.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • One skillet, one pot. The chicken sears and the sauce builds in the same pan, so the browned bits from the chicken become flavor in the sauce.
  • The sauce clings. Penne’s ridges and tube shape trap the garlic-parmesan cream, so every bite carries sauce instead of leaving it at the bottom of the bowl.
  • Real 30 minutes. The pasta boils while the chicken cooks — the timeline overlaps on purpose, exactly like our cajun chicken pasta.

Ingredients You'll Need

Chicken breast keeps it lean, but boneless thighs are even more forgiving and stay juicier if your stove runs hot. Heavy cream makes the sauce silky without any flour; if you only have half-and-half, see the FAQ below for the adjustment. Parmesan should be grated fresh off the block — pre-shredded cheese is coated in anti-caking starch and melts grainy. Italian seasoning and smoked paprika season the chicken crust; swap in Cajun seasoning if you like heat. A handful of baby spinach or halved cherry tomatoes stirred in at the end adds color and freshness without extra work.

  • tsp smoked paprika — a key ingredient in this recipe, worth using the real thing where possible.
  • tsp kosher salt — a key ingredient in this recipe, worth using the real thing where possible.

  • Tongs
  • Large pot for boiling pasta

Instructions

  2. 2

    Toss the chicken pieces with Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, ½ tsp salt, and the pepper.

  3. 3

    Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high; sear the chicken in a single layer 3 minutes without moving, then flip and cook 3-4 minutes more to 165°F (74°C). Transfer to a plate.

  4. 4

    Lower the heat to medium; melt the butter and cook the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.

  5. 5

    Pour in the heavy cream, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.

Yes — rigatoni, ziti, or fusilli all work well because they hold the creamy sauce in their ridges. Adjust the cooking time to the package directions and keep the pasta al dente, since it finishes in the hot sauce.

Cut the breast into even 1-inch pieces, don't crowd the pan, and pull the chicken off the heat as soon as it reaches 165°F (74°C). It rests while you build the sauce and finishes warming through at the end.

Absolutely. Skip the searing step, shred about 3 cups of rotisserie chicken, and stir it in during the last 2–3 minutes so it heats through without drying out.

The pan was too hot when the parmesan went in. Always pull the skillet off direct heat, let the sauce stop bubbling, then stir in finely grated parmesan a handful at a time.

item.title: Easy Coconut Chicken Curry
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Rich, fragrant coconut chicken curry with tender chicken thighs simmered in a creamy coconut milk sauce with red curry paste, warm spices, and fresh lime — ready in 35 minutes in one pan.
item.content:encoded:
This coconut chicken curry is everything you want on a weeknight — rich, warmly spiced, and absolutely packed with flavor, all from one pan in just 35 minutes. Tender chicken thighs simmer in a creamy, fragrant coconut milk sauce that tastes like you spent hours in the kitchen, even though you absolutely did not.

I grew up eating curry at a little Thai spot near our apartment, and I spent years trying to recreate that flavor at home. The secret? It's not some rare ingredient you have to hunt down — it's all about how you treat the curry paste. Once I figured that out, this became the most-requested dinner in our house. My husband asks for it at least once a week, and my kids who once claimed they "don't like spicy food" now go back for seconds. That tells you everything you need to know.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • One pan, 35 minutes — weeknight dinner without the weeknight stress
  • Rich, restaurant-quality flavor — thanks to the curry paste blooming technique
  • Customizable heat level — mild, medium, or spicy — you're in control
  • All ingredients at US grocery stores — no specialty store required
  • Meal prep champion — tastes even better the next day as the flavors develop

About the Key Ingredients

Everything in this recipe is available at a standard US supermarket — Kroger, Whole Foods, Walmart, Trader Joe's. Here's what you're working with and where to find anything unfamiliar:

  • Red curry paste — this is the backbone of the dish. Find it in the Asian foods aisle of any major US grocery store. Maesri and Thai Kitchen are the most common brands on shelves. Thai Kitchen is milder and works great if you're cooking for kids or spice-sensitive folks. Maesri has a bolder, more complex flavor.
  • Full-fat coconut milk — please use full-fat, not light. The richness of the fat is what gives the sauce that luxurious body. Thai Kitchen, Chaokoh, and store brands all work well. Shake the can before opening.
  • Fish sauce — don't let it intimidate you. It's at Whole Foods, Kroger, most Asian grocery stores, and increasingly at Walmart in the Asian foods aisle. Red Boat and Tiparos are popular brands. It smells pungent in the bottle but mellows completely when cooked, adding a deep savory richness you can't get any other way. Don't skip it. If you absolutely must, soy sauce is the substitute, but the depth won't be quite the same.
  • Coconut oil — for searing and cooking. It pairs beautifully with the curry flavors. Substitute vegetable oil if you don't have it.
  • Fresh ginger — sold in the produce section near garlic and onions. A knob of ginger lasts weeks in the fridge. Grate it fresh — it's a world apart from dried ginger powder.

One Key Technique: Blooming the Curry Paste

The single most important thing you'll do in this recipe is add the red curry paste to the pan and cook it for a full minute before adding any liquid. This is called "blooming" — and it's the difference between a curry that tastes flat and a curry that tastes like it came from a Thai restaurant. The heat activates and deepens the fat-soluble compounds in the paste, releasing their full aromatic potential. You'll know it's working when the paste turns slightly darker and your kitchen smells incredible. Don't rush this step, and don't add liquid too soon.

Easy Coconut Chicken Curry

Tender chicken thighs in a rich, creamy coconut milk and red curry sauce — one pan, 35 minutes, better than takeout.

Prep 10 min
Cook 25 min
Total 35 min
Serves 4
Calories 490 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Sear the chicken. Heat coconut oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add chicken thighs and sear 4–5 minutes per side until deep golden brown on each side. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked through yet — it'll finish in the sauce. Remove to a plate and set aside.

  2. 2

    Build the aromatics. In the same pan, add diced onion and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the red curry paste and stir constantly for a full minute — you want it to sizzle, darken slightly, and coat everything. This step is what makes the curry taste deep and complex.

  3. 3

    Add the coconut milk. Pour in the full-fat coconut milk and chicken broth, stirring to fully incorporate the curry paste into the liquid. Add the fish sauce and sugar. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.

  4. 4

    Simmer with the chicken and vegetables. Return the seared chicken and any resting juices to the pan. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. In the last 5 minutes, add the sliced red bell pepper. In the very last minute, stir in the baby spinach and let it wilt into the sauce.

  5. 5

    Finish and serve. Remove from heat. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the curry and taste — adjust salt or add more fish sauce as needed. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro (or parsley). Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice or with warm naan bread.

Pro Tips for Perfect Coconut Chicken Curry

  • Don't skip the curry paste bloom. Cooking the paste in oil for a full minute before adding liquid is the single biggest flavor upgrade in this recipe. Resist the urge to rush it.
  • Use full-fat coconut milk. Light coconut milk will give you a thin, watery curry. The fat in full-fat coconut milk is what creates that creamy, restaurant-style sauce.
  • Where to find red curry paste: It's in the Asian foods aisle of virtually every US grocery store — Kroger, Walmart, Whole Foods, Target. Maesri and Thai Kitchen are common brands. Thai Kitchen tends to be milder.
  • Fish sauce at US stores: Look for it in the Asian foods aisle at Whole Foods, Kroger, most Walmarts, and any Asian grocery store. Red Boat and Tiparos are reliable brands.
  • Adjust heat to taste. Start with 1 tablespoon of red curry paste if cooking for spice-sensitive eaters, up to 3 tablespoons if you like it fiery.

Variations to Try

  • Shrimp coconut curry: Swap chicken for 1 lb large shrimp. Add shrimp in the last 3–4 minutes of cooking — they cook very fast and will turn rubbery if overcooked.
  • Vegetarian version: Replace chicken with 1 can drained chickpeas and 1 cup cubed sweet potato. Add sweet potato with the coconut milk and chickpeas in the last 5 minutes.
  • Green curry: Use green curry paste instead of red for a brighter, slightly different flavor profile. Reduce to 1.5 tablespoons as green paste can be spicier.
  • Add bamboo shoots: A drained can of bamboo shoots stirred in with the broth adds an authentic Thai restaurant texture.
  • Peanut butter twist: Stir 1 tablespoon of natural peanut butter into the sauce for extra richness and nutty depth.

Serving Suggestions

Coconut chicken curry is incredibly versatile. Here's how to make it a full meal:

  • Steamed jasmine rice — the classic pairing, soaks up the sauce beautifully
  • Warm naan bread — for scooping and mopping up every drop of sauce
  • Cauliflower rice — for a lower-carb option that still works wonderfully
  • Rice noodles — for a Thai-noodle-style bowl
  • A simple cucumber salad on the side to cool things down
  • Extra fresh lime wedges on the table — a squeeze brightens every bite

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days. The curry actually tastes better the next day as flavors deepen overnight.

Freezer

Freeze for up to 3 months in a freezer-safe container. Coconut milk curries freeze surprisingly well. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheat

Warm gently in a skillet over medium-low heat, adding a splash of coconut milk or water to loosen the sauce. Stir gently to recombine. Microwave works in a pinch — cover and heat in 1-minute intervals.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is red curry paste?

Red curry paste is a concentrated blend of red chilies, lemongrass, galangal, garlic, shallots, kaffir lime zest, and shrimp paste (some brands are vegan — check the label). It's the flavor foundation of Thai red curry. You'll find it in the Asian foods aisle of most US grocery stores. Thai Kitchen is the most widely available brand and is milder in heat. Maesri is more authentic and bolder in flavor. Both work great in this recipe.

Can I use light coconut milk?

Technically yes, but I really recommend against it. Light coconut milk has significantly less fat, which means your sauce will be thin and watery rather than rich and creamy. If you're watching calories, the better trade-off is to use full-fat coconut milk and eat a slightly smaller serving — you'll be far more satisfied by the flavor and texture. Full-fat coconut milk is also more filling, so you tend to eat less overall.

Is this curry spicy?

With 2 tablespoons of Thai Kitchen red curry paste, this curry is mild to medium — there's warmth but it won't set your mouth on fire. Use 1 tablespoon for a very mild curry, 3 tablespoons if you want more heat. The coconut milk also naturally tones down the spice level. Maesri curry paste is spicier than Thai Kitchen, so use slightly less if switching brands.

Where can I find fish sauce in US stores?

Fish sauce is much easier to find than most people expect! Look in the Asian foods aisle at Whole Foods, Kroger, Publix, most Walmarts, and Target stores. Any Asian grocery store will definitely carry it. Popular brands include Red Boat (premium, worth it), Tiparos, and Thai Kitchen. If you truly cannot find it, soy sauce is the substitute — use 1 tablespoon soy sauce in place of 1 tablespoon fish sauce. The flavor is different but still great.

Toss vigorously, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is silky and coats every strand. Serve immediately with fresh basil.

item.title: Creamy Tuscan Shrimp
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Juicy shrimp in a rich sun-dried tomato and spinach cream sauce, ready in 20 minutes.
item.content:encoded:
This creamy Tuscan shrimp is the most impressive 20-minute dinner you'll ever make. Plump, perfectly seared shrimp swimming in a rich, velvety sauce of sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, Parmesan, and fresh spinach — it looks like it took an hour and tastes like it cost $40 at a restaurant.

Tuscan-inspired dishes have taken over American home kitchens in the last few years, and for good reason — the flavor combination of sun-dried tomatoes, cream, garlic, and Parmesan is absolutely addictive. The sun-dried tomatoes add an intense sweetness and depth that makes the sauce taste complex without any real effort. I've made this for dinner parties where guests couldn't believe it took less than 20 minutes.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • 20 minutes start to finish — impressive speed for such a sophisticated dish
  • Restaurant quality at home — the sun-dried tomato cream sauce is genuinely spectacular
  • One pan — easy cleanup for such an elegant meal
  • Versatile — serve over pasta, rice, or with crusty bread
  • High protein, naturally low-carb — as written, under 10g carbs per serving

Finding Your Ingredients

Shrimp: Look for "large" or "jumbo" shrimp, already peeled and deveined to save time. Frozen shrimp works perfectly — thaw overnight in the fridge or under cold running water for 10 minutes. Available at every US grocery store. Trader Joe's and Costco both have excellent frozen shrimp at great prices.

Sun-dried tomatoes: Buy sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil (not the dry-packed kind). They're softer, more flavorful, and ready to use. Available in the Italian foods or condiment aisle at Whole Foods, Kroger, and most major grocery stores. The oil they're packed in is also great for cooking — don't waste it.

Heavy cream: Same as heavy whipping cream at any US store. This is what makes the sauce velvety rather than watery.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet (12-inch) — stainless steel or cast iron
  • Tongs for the shrimp
  • Wooden spoon for the sauce

Creamy Tuscan Shrimp

Perfectly seared shrimp in a rich sun-dried tomato, Parmesan, and spinach cream sauce. One pan, 20 minutes.

Prep5 min
Cook15 min
Total20 min
Serves4
Calories420 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Season and sear the shrimp. Pat shrimp completely dry. Season with salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add shrimp in a single layer and cook 1–2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and curled into a C-shape (not an O-shape, which means overcooked). Transfer to a plate immediately.

  2. 2

    Build the sauce base. Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 60 seconds until the garlic is golden and fragrant. Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom.

  3. 3

    Create the cream sauce. Pour in the heavy cream and stir to combine with the broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add the Parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes if using. Stir until the Parmesan is fully melted and the sauce is smooth.

  4. 4

    Wilt the spinach. Add the baby spinach in handfuls and stir until just wilted — this takes about 1–2 minutes. Don't overcook; it should be bright green and just collapsed.

  5. 5

    Finish and serve. Return the shrimp to the pan along with any juices on the plate. Toss gently in the sauce and heat for just 30 seconds — shrimp overcook very quickly. Taste and adjust salt. Garnish with fresh basil and serve immediately over pasta, rice, or with bread.

Pro Tips for Perfect Tuscan Shrimp

  • Don't overcook the shrimp. Shrimp go from perfect to rubbery in 30 seconds. The moment they're pink and curled (a C-shape), they're done. Take them out immediately.
  • Dry the shrimp. Moisture on shrimp surfaces creates steam instead of a sear. Pat with paper towels before cooking.
  • Use freshly grated Parmesan. Pre-shredded Parmesan from a bag contains cellulose that prevents it from melting smoothly. Buy a block and grate it yourself — it makes a silkier sauce.
  • Save the sun-dried tomato oil. The oil the tomatoes are packed in is incredibly flavorful. Use it instead of plain olive oil to cook the garlic for even more Tuscan depth.

Variations

  • Tuscan chicken: Replace shrimp with thinly sliced chicken breast — pound to even thickness, sear 4–5 minutes per side, then make the same sauce.
  • Dairy-free: Use full-fat coconut cream instead of heavy cream and nutritional yeast instead of Parmesan for a dairy-free version.
  • Add artichokes: Quarter-cup of marinated artichoke hearts added with the sun-dried tomatoes is a classic Tuscan addition.
  • Mushroom version: Add 8 oz (225g) sliced cremini mushrooms after the garlic, cook 3 minutes, then proceed with the sauce.

Serving Suggestions

  • Fettuccine or linguine — toss the pasta directly in the sauce for a full Tuscan pasta dish
  • Over white rice or cauliflower rice
  • With crusty sourdough or a French baguette for sauce scooping
  • Over polenta for a Southern Italian feel
  • With a simple arugula salad dressed in lemon and olive oil

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store up to 2 days. Shrimp texture degrades quickly.

Freezer

Not recommended — cream sauces and cooked shrimp don't freeze well.

Reheat

Warm gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of cream. Shrimp overcook easily when reheated.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use frozen shrimp for this recipe?

Absolutely — frozen shrimp is what most home cooks use and it's perfectly fine. Thaw it overnight in the fridge, or place in a colander under cold running water for 5–10 minutes. The key is to pat it VERY dry after thawing before cooking. Frozen shrimp releases more water than fresh and needs to be well-dried for a good sear.

What does "peeled and deveined" mean?

The shell is removed (peeled) and the dark digestive tract running along the back of the shrimp is removed (deveined). Most shrimp sold in US grocery stores comes this way. Look for bags labeled "EZ peel," "peeled and deveined," or "P&D" at Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, or in the frozen seafood section of any major grocery store.

Can I substitute half-and-half for heavy cream?

You can, but the sauce will be thinner and less rich. Half-and-half is 12% fat vs 36% fat in heavy cream — the lower fat content means less body and a tendency for the sauce to separate if it gets too hot. If you use half-and-half, keep the heat at a very low simmer and don't let it boil.

Where can I find sun-dried tomatoes in US stores?

In the Italian foods or condiment aisle at any major grocery store. Most commonly stocked brands: Trader Joe's has their own excellent version, California Sun Dry is widely available at Whole Foods and Kroger, and Alessi and DeLallo are found at most supermarkets. Look for "sun-dried tomatoes in olive oil" — the oil-packed ones are much better than dry-packed for this recipe.

item.title: Crispy Baked Chicken Wings
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Shatteringly crispy baked chicken wings using the baking powder technique — no frying required.
item.content:encoded:
I'm going to tell you a secret that changed the way I make chicken wings forever: baking powder — not baking soda, not any special coating — is all you need to get oven-baked wings that are genuinely, shatteringly crispy. No frying. No vat of oil. No mess. Just wings that come out of the oven with that crackle you'd expect from a restaurant.

The science is simple: baking powder is alkaline, and when you coat chicken skin with it and bake at high heat, it raises the pH of the skin's surface. This breaks down the proteins, draws out moisture, and creates thousands of tiny bubbles that make the skin incredibly crunchy and light. It's the same technique used by serious wing spots — and once you know it, you'll never make wings any other way.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • Genuinely crispy — the baking powder technique creates a shatter-crisp crust that rivals fried wings
  • No frying — no oil splatter, no smell, no danger, no cleanup nightmare
  • Crowd-pleaser — great for game day, parties, or family dinner night
  • Versatile sauce options — honey garlic, buffalo, BBQ, or plain with dipping sauce
  • Make-ahead friendly — season and refrigerate overnight for even crispier results

The Baking Powder Science (Why It Works)

This is genuinely fascinating food science that makes a real difference. Here's what happens step by step:

  • Baking powder is alkaline (high pH). Chicken skin is slightly acidic.
  • When alkaline baking powder coats acidic skin, it neutralizes the acids and raises the skin's pH.
  • Higher pH speeds up the Maillard reaction — the browning reaction that creates flavor and crispiness — at lower temperatures.
  • The baking powder also reacts with moisture in the skin to create small CO₂ bubbles, making the skin puffed and airy rather than dense and chewy.

Critical warning: Use BAKING POWDER, not baking soda. They are completely different ingredients. Baking soda is much stronger and will make your wings taste metallic and soapy. Check the label carefully — baking powder is typically in a small yellow can (Clabber Girl or Davis brand at any US grocery store).

The Two-Temperature Oven Technique

The second secret to these wings is the two-temperature approach: start low (250°F / 120°C) then finish high (425°F / 220°C).

  • Low temperature first — 20 minutes at 250°F gently renders the fat beneath the skin without cooking the meat. Less fat under the skin = crispier skin.
  • High temperature finish — the remaining 40-45 minutes at 425°F is where the magic happens. The now-dry, fat-rendered skin crisps up and turns golden brown.

Skipping the low temperature step and just baking at high heat the whole time is one of the most common mistakes — the fat doesn't have time to render and you end up with greasy wings.

Kitchen Tools You'll Need

  • Large rimmed baking sheet (at least 18x13 inch)
  • Wire rack — this is important. It elevates the wings so air circulates underneath, preventing the bottom from steaming. Available at any kitchen store, Walmart, or Amazon.
  • Aluminum foil (for easier cleanup)
  • Large bowl for tossing
  • Small saucepan for the sauce

Crispy Baked Chicken Wings

Shatteringly crispy oven wings using the baking powder technique. Tossed in a sticky honey garlic sauce. No frying, no compromise on crunch.

Prep10 min
Cook60 min
Total70 min
Serves4
Calories380 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Wings

Honey Garlic Sauce

Instructions

  1. 1

    Dry the wings thoroughly. Pat wings completely dry on all sides using paper towels. This is the most important step — any moisture prevents crisping. In a large bowl, toss wings with baking powder, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Every piece should have a thin, even coating.

  2. 2

    Set on a rack. Arrange wings skin-side up in a single layer on a wire rack set over a foil-lined baking sheet. Leave space between each wing. For maximum crispiness, refrigerate uncovered for 30 minutes to 8 hours — the fridge dehydrates the skin even further. This step is optional but highly recommended.

  3. 3

    Start low. Preheat oven to 250°F / 120°C. Bake wings at this low temperature for 20 minutes. This slowly renders the fat under the skin, which is key to a crispy result. Don't skip this step.

  4. 4

    Blast at high heat. Increase oven temperature to 425°F / 220°C. Continue baking for 40–45 minutes, flipping wings at the 20-minute mark. The wings are done when they are deep golden brown and the skin sounds crisp when you tap it. The underside should be equally golden.

  5. 5

    Make the sauce and toss. While the wings finish baking, melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add honey, soy sauce, and hot sauce (if using). Simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Toss hot wings in the sauce in a large bowl just before serving — tossing too early softens the crispy skin.

The Secrets to Maximum Crispiness

  • Baking POWDER not baking soda. Print this, tattoo it, do not confuse them. One makes wings crispy. The other makes wings taste like chemicals.
  • Wire rack is non-negotiable. Wings sitting directly on the pan steam in their own fat. The rack lets hot air circulate on all sides.
  • Refrigerate uncovered. Even 30 minutes in the fridge dramatically dries the skin and makes the final result crisper.
  • Toss in sauce right before serving. Sauce applied too early makes the skin soft. Add sauce in the last 60 seconds before the wings hit the table.

Sauce Variations

  • Classic buffalo: Toss in Frank's RedHot mixed with melted butter (2:1 ratio). The definitive American wing sauce.
  • BBQ: Brush with your favorite BBQ sauce in the last 10 minutes of baking for a caramelized finish.
  • Lemon pepper: Skip the sauce and toss in melted butter + lemon zest + cracked black pepper. Clean, bright, and addictive.
  • Plain and crispy: Serve with blue cheese or ranch dipping sauce on the side — the crispy skin needs nothing else.

Serving Suggestions

  • Classic celery and carrot sticks alongside blue cheese or ranch dressing for dipping
  • Served with coleslaw and corn on the cob for a full game-day spread
  • Over rice with extra honey garlic sauce drizzled over for a dinner-style presentation
  • As an appetizer platter at parties — make a double batch, they disappear fast

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store cooked wings for up to 4 days. Keep sauce separate.

Freezer

Freeze cooked unsauced wings up to 3 months.

Reheat

Re-crisp in the oven at 400°F for 10 minutes. Microwave makes them soft.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why baking powder and not baking soda?

They're completely different chemicals that behave differently on food. Baking powder (sodium bicarbonate + cream of tartar) is much milder and works by raising the skin's pH slightly, which promotes browning and creates a dry, crispy texture. Baking soda (pure sodium bicarbonate) is much stronger — using it on wings creates a metallic, soapy taste. Always baking POWDER for this recipe.

Do I really need a wire rack?

Yes, if you want truly crispy wings. Without a rack, the bottom of the wings sits in the fat that renders out during cooking. That fat steams the underside, making it soft instead of crispy. The rack is available at every kitchen store, Walmart, Target, and Amazon for under $15.

Can I use frozen wings?

Yes, but thaw them completely first and make sure they're VERY dry — frozen wings release a lot more moisture. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then pat aggressively with paper towels before tossing in the baking powder mixture. You may need to add 5–10 extra minutes of baking time.

Can I prep these ahead of time?

Absolutely — and it actually improves them. Season the wings and place on the rack, then refrigerate uncovered for up to 24 hours before baking. The extended fridge time dries the skin even further. This is the ultimate make-ahead trick for parties.

Nutrition Information

Per serving (approximately 6–7 wings with sauce). Values are estimates.

item.title: Crispy Honey Garlic Salmon
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Crispy pan-seared salmon with a sticky honey garlic glaze, ready in 17 minutes. The fastest weeknight dinner that tastes like a restaurant dish.
item.content:encoded:
This crispy honey garlic salmon is the recipe I make when I want something that looks and tastes impressive but takes less time than ordering delivery. Crispy on the outside, flaky and tender inside, coated in a sticky sweet-savory glaze — it hits every note perfectly in just 17 minutes.

I've made a lot of salmon recipes over the years, but this glaze is the one that gets people asking for the recipe at the dinner table. The secret is cornstarch in the glaze — it thickens quickly under heat and creates that glossy, restaurant-style lacquer on the fish. The sesame oil adds a subtle nuttiness that ties the whole dish together.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • 17 minutes start to finish — the fastest dinner on this site
  • 5 ingredients for the glaze — all pantry staples
  • Crispy exterior, flaky interior — the technique makes all the difference
  • Healthy and satisfying — packed with omega-3s and protein
  • Impressive enough for guests — looks like a restaurant dish

Choosing Your Salmon

The best salmon for this recipe is skin-on Atlantic or Pacific salmon fillets, each about 6–8 oz (170–225g). Here's where to buy the best salmon in the US:

  • Whole Foods — excellent fresh and frozen options, including wild-caught sockeye and Atlantic farmed
  • Trader Joe's — their frozen wild-caught salmon is fantastic quality for the price and thaws perfectly overnight
  • Costco / Sam's Club — buy a whole side and portion it yourself for the best value
  • Kroger / Publix / any major grocery — fresh salmon at the seafood counter is great; just ask when it came in

Wild-caught vs. farmed: Both work in this recipe. Wild-caught (sockeye, coho) tends to be leaner and more deeply flavored. Farmed Atlantic salmon is fattier, which means it's more forgiving to cook and stays very moist.

About the Honey Garlic Glaze

This glaze is four ingredients that you almost certainly already have:

  • Honey — any kind works. Clover honey (the standard US grocery store variety) is perfect.
  • Soy sauce — use low-sodium so the glaze doesn't get too salty as it reduces. Kikkoman is the most widely available brand in the US.
  • Garlic — fresh minced cloves, please. The flavor difference versus jarred garlic is very noticeable in a quick-cooking glaze like this.
  • Sesame oil — toasted sesame oil (the darker, fragrant kind) adds incredible depth. Find it in the Asian foods aisle at any US grocery store.
  • Cornstarch — the secret to a glossy, sticky glaze that coats the fish beautifully instead of sliding off.

Crispy Honey Garlic Salmon

Crispy pan-seared salmon with a sticky honey garlic glaze. Five simple ingredients. Seventeen minutes. Pure weeknight magic.

Prep 5 min
Cook 12 min
Total 17 min
Serves 2
Calories 390 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

2 servings

Salmon

Honey Garlic Glaze

Garnish

Instructions

  1. 1

    Make the glaze. Whisk together honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, lemon juice, sesame oil, and cornstarch in a small bowl until the cornstarch is fully dissolved and there are no lumps. Set aside near the stove — you'll need it quickly.

  2. 2

    Prep the salmon. Pat salmon fillets completely dry with paper towels — moisture is the enemy of a crispy crust. Season both sides with salt and pepper. If your fillets are cold from the fridge, let them sit at room temperature for 10 minutes.

  3. 3

    Sear flesh-side down first. Heat oil in a non-stick or stainless skillet over medium-high heat until hot and shimmering — a drop of water should sizzle immediately. Place salmon flesh-side DOWN (not skin side) and press gently with a spatula for 10 seconds to ensure full contact. Cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until the sides of the salmon are turning opaque halfway up.

  4. 4

    Flip and add the glaze. Flip the salmon so it's now skin-side down. Immediately pour the glaze over and around the fillets. The glaze will bubble aggressively — that's perfect. Spoon the glaze back over the top of the salmon repeatedly as it cooks. Cook 3–4 more minutes, basting constantly, until the glaze is thick and syrupy and the salmon flakes easily when tested with a fork.

  5. 5

    Rest and serve. Transfer salmon to plates. Spoon any remaining glaze from the pan over the top. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced green onions. Serve with lemon wedges and your chosen sides.

The Secrets to Perfectly Crispy Salmon

  • DRY the fish. Moisture on the surface creates steam, which prevents crisping. Paper towels are your best friend here.
  • Hot pan, cold fish. Wait until the oil is fully shimmering before adding the salmon. A lukewarm pan means steamed fish, not crispy fish.
  • Don't move it. Once the salmon is in the pan, leave it completely alone until it's ready to flip. It will naturally release when it's properly seared.
  • Baste constantly. Once the glaze is in, spoon it over the salmon every 30 seconds. This builds up the glossy lacquer finish.
  • Pull at 130°F / 54°C. Salmon continues cooking after you remove it from heat. If you wait for 145°F, it'll be dry by the time it reaches your plate.

Variations

  • Spicy honey garlic: Add ½ teaspoon sriracha or red pepper flakes to the glaze for a sweet heat version.
  • Ginger version: Add 1 teaspoon of freshly grated ginger to the glaze for a brighter, more aromatic flavor.
  • Orange instead of lemon: Substitute fresh orange juice for the lemon for a sweeter citrus note.
  • Gluten-free: Replace soy sauce with tamari or coconut aminos — same flavor, no gluten.
  • Baked version: Brush salmon with glaze and bake at 400°F / 205°C for 12–15 minutes. Less crispy but more hands-off.

Serving Suggestions

This salmon works with almost any side:

  • Steamed jasmine or basmati rice — the glaze drips into the rice beautifully
  • Roasted broccoli or asparagus (toss in olive oil and roast at 425°F while the salmon cooks)
  • A simple cucumber and sesame salad for a fresh contrast
  • Mashed potatoes for a heartier, comfort-food style plate
  • Zucchini noodles for a light, low-carb option

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store cooked salmon in an airtight container for up to 2 days. The crust softens on storage — that's normal.

Freezer

Cooked salmon freezes for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.

Reheat

Reheat in a covered skillet over low heat with a small splash of water for 3 minutes. Avoid the microwave — it overcooks salmon and makes it rubbery.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I eat the skin on honey garlic salmon?

When cooked properly, salmon skin becomes deliciously crispy — it's arguably the best part! If your skin is crispy, eat it. If it's soft (which can happen on the second day after storage), it's easy to peel off before eating. The skin is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, so there's nutritional value too.

Can I use frozen salmon?

Yes, but you must thaw it completely first and pat it VERY dry. Frozen salmon releases more water than fresh as it thaws — any remaining moisture will steam the fish instead of searing it. For best results, thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

How do I know when salmon is done?

The best method is a fork test: insert a fork at the thickest part and twist gently — perfectly cooked salmon flakes easily into layers. For precision, use an instant-read thermometer: 125–130°F (52–54°C) for medium (slightly translucent in the very center), or 145°F (63°C) for fully cooked (what the FDA recommends). I prefer 130°F for maximum juiciness.

Can I make this without sesame oil?

Sesame oil adds a lot of flavor, but yes — you can skip it and the recipe still works well. You can substitute with a few drops of olive oil or simply leave it out. If you want to buy sesame oil, it's in the Asian foods aisle at Walmart, Kroger, or any US grocery store (Kadoya and Lee Kum Kee are common brands).

What's the difference between Atlantic and wild-caught salmon?

Atlantic salmon is almost always farmed — it's fattier, has a milder flavor, and is more forgiving to cook (the fat keeps it moist). Wild-caught (sockeye, coho, king/chinook) is leaner, more intensely flavored, and bright orange-red in color. Both are excellent in this recipe. If you're new to cooking salmon, start with Atlantic — it's harder to dry out.

item.content:encoded:
This crockpot marry me chicken pasta is about to become your new favorite slow cooker dinner. Juicy shredded chicken, a luscious sun-dried tomato cream sauce, tender pasta, and wilted spinach — all made with just 15 minutes of prep. It’s the kind of meal that has your family saying “yes!” before you even finish serving it.

This crockpot marry me chicken pasta recipe uses American flavors and comes together with everyday ingredients — no special trip to a specialty store required.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • Truly hands-off: 15 minutes of prep, then let the crockpot do everything
  • One-pot wonder: Almost everything cooks in the slow cooker
  • Crowd-pleaser: Creamy, rich, and packed with flavor — even picky eaters love it
  • Perfect for meal prep: Makes 6 generous servings that reheat beautifully
  • Restaurant quality at home: Sun-dried tomatoes + Parmesan = incredible depth of flavor

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket. A few notes on what makes each ingredient work:

  • Chicken breasts: Boneless skinless — they shred perfectly after slow cooking. Thighs work great too
  • Sun-dried tomatoes: Use oil-packed for the best flavor. They’re the secret ingredient that makes it “marry me” worthy
  • Heavy cream: Creates that ultra-rich, velvety sauce. Don’t substitute with milk — it will be too thin
  • Parmesan cheese: Freshly grated melts better than pre-shredded and gives the sauce incredible depth
  • Fresh spinach: Stirred in at the end for color and a fresh bite
  • Don’t overcook the pasta. Cook it 1 minute under the package directions since it keeps softening in the warm sauce
  • Use the low setting if possible. Lower, slower cooking makes the chicken even more tender and flavorful
  • Shred the chicken finely. The more shredded, the better it absorbs the sauce
  • Let it rest before serving. 5–10 minutes on WARM allows the sauce to thicken to the perfect consistency
  • Season at the end. Parmesan is salty — always taste before adding extra salt

  • 6-quart slow cooker
  • Two forks for shredding
  • Large pot for boiling pasta
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Sharp knife and cutting board

Crockpot Marry Me Chicken Pasta

Prep 15 min

This creamy garlic chicken is the kind of weeknight dinner you'll make on repeat. Juicy, golden chicken thighs bathed in a velvety garlic cream sauce — all done in one pan, in just 30 minutes. The sauce is so good you'll want to pour it over everything.

I first made this on a rainy Tuesday when the fridge had almost nothing in it. Six cloves of garlic, some heavy cream, chicken thighs — and it turned out to be one of the most requested dinners in our house. It's the recipe I give to every friend who says they "can't cook," because if you can sear chicken and stir a sauce, you've got this.

  • One pan, easy cleanup — fewer dishes, more enjoying your evening
  • Ready in 30 minutes — faster than ordering delivery
  • Rich, restaurant-quality sauce — made with everyday pantry staples
  • Budget-friendly — chicken thighs are inexpensive and stay juicy
  • Family-approved — even picky eaters love the creamy sauce

Ingredients You'll Need

Everything here is available at any major supermarket — Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, Kroger, or even your local grocery store. Here's what makes each ingredient special:

  • Chicken thighs — boneless, skinless. Thighs stay juicier than breasts under heat. Look for them in the meat section next to chicken breasts.
  • Heavy cream — this is the same as heavy whipping cream you'll find at any US store. It gives the sauce that rich, velvety body.
  • Fresh garlic — please use fresh cloves, not the jarred kind. The difference in a dish like this is night and day.
  • Chicken broth — low-sodium works great. It deglazes the pan and adds depth without making the sauce too salty.
  • Italian seasoning — a pre-mixed blend (basil, oregano, thyme, rosemary) found in the spice aisle of every US grocery store.

Kitchen Tools

  • Large skillet or cast iron pan (12-inch / 30cm works perfectly)
  • Tongs
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Instant-read meat thermometer (recommended)
  • Garlic press or sharp knife for mincing

Easy Creamy Garlic Chicken

Golden pan-seared chicken thighs in a rich garlic cream sauce. One pan. 30 minutes. Pure weeknight magic.

Prep 10 min
Cook 20 min
Total 30 min
Serves 4
Calories 480 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Season the chicken. Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels — this is the key to a golden crust. Season generously on both sides with salt, black pepper, paprika, and Italian seasoning.

  2. 2

    Sear to golden perfection. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add chicken smooth-side down and press lightly to ensure full contact with the pan. Sear undisturbed for 5 minutes until deep golden brown. Flip and cook 4 more minutes. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.

  3. 3

    Build the garlic base. Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Once melted, add minced garlic and stir constantly for 60 seconds until golden and fragrant. Watch it closely — burnt garlic turns bitter fast.

  4. 4

    Deglaze and add cream. Pour in chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon — those browned bits (called "fond") are pure flavor. Pour in the heavy cream, stir to combine, and bring to a gentle simmer.

  5. 5

    Finish and serve. Return chicken and any resting juices to the pan. Simmer on medium-low for 5–7 minutes, spooning sauce over the chicken, until the sauce thickens to coat a spoon and chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C. Taste and adjust salt. Garnish with parsley and Parmesan. Serve right away.

Pro Tips for Perfect Creamy Garlic Chicken

  • Dry the chicken. Patting it dry with paper towels removes surface moisture, giving you a golden sear instead of steaming the chicken in its own liquid.
  • Don't move the chicken. Resist the urge to poke or shift it during searing. It will naturally release when it's ready to flip.
  • Room temperature chicken. Take chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking for more even cooking throughout.
  • Thicken the sauce. If your sauce is too thin, mix 1 teaspoon cornstarch with 2 teaspoons cold water and stir it in. It thickens in seconds.
  • Don't boil the cream. Keep it at a gentle simmer — a rolling boil can cause the sauce to separate.

Variations to Try

  • Dairy-free: Replace heavy cream with full-fat coconut cream. The flavor is slightly different but equally rich and delicious.
  • Gluten-free: This recipe is naturally gluten-free as written — just double-check your chicken broth label.
  • Spicy version: Add ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes with the garlic for a gentle heat that plays beautifully with the cream.
  • Sun-dried tomato: Stir in 2 tablespoons of chopped sun-dried tomatoes with the garlic for a Tuscan twist.
  • Mushroom garlic chicken: Add 8 oz (225g) sliced mushrooms after the garlic and cook for 3 minutes before adding the broth.

Serving Suggestions

This saucy chicken pairs beautifully with anything that can soak up that incredible cream sauce:

  • Mashed potatoes (the classic choice — the sauce acts like a gravy)
  • Pasta (linguine or fettuccine work great)
  • White rice or cauliflower rice for a lighter option
  • Crusty bread for sauce-scooping
  • Roasted asparagus or green beans on the side
  • Steamed broccoli (kids love dipping it in the sauce)

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

Freezer

Cream sauces can separate when frozen. Best eaten fresh or refrigerated. If freezing, store up to 2 months and stir well when reheating.

Reheat

Warm gently in a skillet over low heat, adding a splash of cream or broth to loosen the sauce. Avoid the microwave if possible — it can make the chicken rubbery.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use chicken breasts instead of thighs?

Yes! Chicken breasts work fine, but they cook faster and can dry out more easily. Pound them to an even ½-inch thickness, and reduce the searing time to 3–4 minutes per side. Use a meat thermometer to hit 165°F / 74°C exactly — don't go over.

Can I make this ahead of time for meal prep?

Absolutely. This reheats beautifully over 4 days. Store the chicken and sauce together in an airtight container. When reheating, add a splash of chicken broth to the pan to bring the sauce back to its original silky consistency.

What can I substitute for heavy cream?

Half-and-half will work but gives a thinner sauce. Full-fat coconut cream is the best dairy-free substitute. Avoid milk or light cream — the sauce won't thicken properly and may separate.

Why is my cream sauce not thickening?

The sauce thickens as it reduces — it needs 5–7 minutes of gentle simmering. Make sure you're not cooking on too high a heat (this causes it to boil too fast and can separate). If you need it thicker quickly, mix 1 tsp cornstarch with 2 tsp cold water and stir it in — it'll thicken within a minute.

Where can I find Italian seasoning in US grocery stores?

Italian seasoning is in the spice aisle of every major US grocery store — Kroger, Walmart, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's. McCormick and Spice Islands are the most common brands. It's a pre-mixed blend of basil, oregano, thyme, and rosemary.

Can I add vegetables to this dish?

Yes! Baby spinach wilts beautifully into the sauce in the last 2 minutes of cooking. Sliced mushrooms can be added after the garlic step. Cherry tomatoes added with the cream burst and add brightness to the dish.

item.title: Garlic Butter Steak Bites
item.dc:creator: mars
item.description: Tender sirloin cubes seared in a hot skillet and finished with garlic herb butter — a 15-minute dinner that tastes like a steakhouse.
item.content:encoded:
These garlic butter steak bites are proof that the most impressive dinners are often the simplest ones. Tender sirloin cubes, seared at high heat until caramelized and crusty on the outside, then finished in a cloud of foaming garlic herb butter — all in 15 minutes flat. This tastes like a steakhouse, costs a fraction of the price, and you'll be licking the pan.

The secret is a two-stage technique: sear the steak over blazing high heat first to get that deep, brown crust, then add the butter and aromatics at the end. This way the garlic doesn't burn, the herbs stay bright, and the butter coats every piece of steak in a glossy, fragrant sauce. It's a technique used in professional kitchens — and it works perfectly at home in under 15 minutes.

Why You'll Love This Recipe

  • 15 minutes from fridge to table — the fastest impressive dinner on this site
  • Steakhouse flavor at home — high-heat sear + butter basting is the professional technique
  • Crowd-pleaser — works as a weeknight dinner or impressive dinner party dish
  • Low-carb and protein-packed — 42g protein per serving
  • No marinating needed — great quality beef doesn't need it

Best Cut of Beef for Steak Bites

Not all beef is equal for this recipe. Here's your guide to choosing at US grocery stores:

  • Sirloin (top sirloin) — the best balance of tenderness, flavor, and price. Our top recommendation. Available at every grocery store.
  • Ribeye — the most flavorful, most marbled, most expensive. Absolute luxury. Worth it for special occasions.
  • New York strip — similar to sirloin, great texture, slightly less tender than ribeye.
  • Tenderloin (filet mignon cubes) — the most tender cut, very mild flavor, highest price. Best for a special date night.
  • Avoid chuck or round steak for this recipe — they need long cooking to become tender and won't work with the quick-sear method.

Find good quality beef at Whole Foods, Costco, Trader Joe's, or ask the butcher at your local grocery store for a fresh-cut sirloin. Costco has excellent sirloin at the best price per pound.

Kitchen Tools

  • Cast iron skillet (12-inch) — this is the ideal pan for high-heat searing. If you don't have one, a heavy stainless steel skillet works.
  • Tongs — essential for turning the steak bites quickly
  • Instant-read thermometer (optional but helpful)
  • Sharp chef's knife for cutting the steak

Garlic Butter Steak Bites

Juicy, caramelized sirloin cubes finished in garlic herb butter. 15 minutes. No fuss. Pure steak perfection.

Prep5 min
Cook10 min
Total15 min
Serves4
Calories380 kcal
📌 Save to Pinterest

Ingredients

4 servings

Instructions

  1. 1

    Prep the steak. Cut sirloin into 1-inch cubes. Pat every piece completely dry with paper towels — this is the single most important step for getting a good sear. Season very generously with kosher salt and black pepper on all sides. Don't be shy with the seasoning.

  2. 2

    Superheat the pan. Heat a cast iron or heavy skillet over HIGH heat for 2–3 minutes until it's very hot — a drop of water should evaporate instantly. Add the oil. It will shimmer and smoke slightly. This high heat is what creates the dark, caramelized crust.

  3. 3

    Sear in batches. Working in two batches (don't crowd the pan — this causes steaming instead of searing), add the steak cubes in a single layer. Sear undisturbed for 60–90 seconds, then turn each piece and sear the other sides for 30–60 seconds. For medium-rare, internal temperature should be 130–135°F / 54–57°C. Remove first batch to a plate, repeat with second batch.

  4. 4

    Make the garlic herb butter. Reduce heat to medium. Add all the steak bites back to the pan. Add butter, garlic, thyme, and rosemary. As the butter melts and foams, use a spoon to continuously baste the steak bites with the garlic-herb butter for 30–45 seconds.

  5. 5

    Finish and serve. Add Worcestershire sauce and toss everything together quickly. Remove from heat immediately. Transfer to a serving plate, pour any remaining butter from the pan over the top, and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges on the side — a squeeze of lemon over the steak at the table is outstanding.

The Keys to Perfect Steak Bites

  • Dry is everything. Any moisture on the beef surface creates steam, which prevents the crust. Pat with paper towels right before cooking.
  • Cook in batches. Crowding the pan drops the temperature and the beef steams instead of sears. Two batches = much better results.
  • Don't well-done them. Steak bites are at their best at medium-rare (130°F / 54°C) or medium (140°F / 60°C). Cooking past medium makes them chewy and less flavorful.
  • Rest even briefly. Let the steak bites rest on the plate for 2 minutes before eating so the juices redistribute.
  • Add butter last. Butter burns at high heat. Always sear first with oil, then add butter at medium heat to baste.

Variations

  • Mushroom version: Add 8 oz (225g) sliced cremini mushrooms after the first batch of steak and sauté for 3 minutes before making the butter sauce.
  • Cajun style: Season steak bites with Cajun seasoning instead of just salt and pepper for a spicy Southern flavor.
  • Asian-inspired: Replace the rosemary/thyme with ginger, add a teaspoon of sesame oil, and finish with a drizzle of soy sauce instead of Worcestershire.
  • Herb compound butter: Make a compound butter by mixing softened butter with garlic, herbs, and lemon zest — serve a pat on top of the hot steak bites at the table.

Serving Suggestions

  • Garlic mashed potatoes — the classic steakhouse combination
  • Over egg noodles or pasta with the butter sauce drizzled over
  • With roasted asparagus and a simple green salad
  • Over cauliflower mash for a low-carb dinner
  • As a appetizer on toothpicks for dinner parties — they disappear in minutes
  • Served in a warm bowl with steamed white rice

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerator

Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

Freezer

Freeze cooked steak bites up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

Reheat

Warm briefly in a hot skillet with a small knob of butter for 1–2 minutes. Don't microwave — it overcooks beef quickly.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the best way to cut steak for steak bites?

Cut the steak into 1-inch cubes — this size gives you a good crust-to-interior ratio. Cut against the grain of the meat (perpendicular to the muscle fibers) for maximum tenderness. You'll see the grain lines running in one direction — cut across them, not parallel to them.

Can I use pre-cut stew beef for this recipe?

Only if the package specifically says "sirloin stew beef" or "top sirloin." Generic stew beef is usually cut from tougher chuck or round, which needs long braising to become tender. It won't work well with this quick-sear method. Spend the extra bit and buy a sirloin steak to cut yourself.

My steak bites are chewy — what went wrong?

Three likely causes: (1) You used a tough cut like chuck instead of sirloin. (2) You overcooked them — steak bites become chewy past medium (140°F / 60°C). (3) You didn't cut against the grain — even a great cut becomes chewy if cut parallel to the muscle fibers.

Where can I find Worcestershire sauce in US stores?

Worcestershire sauce is in the condiment aisle of every US grocery store — Walmart, Kroger, Publix, Whole Foods. Lea & Perrins is the most widely available brand. It's a dark, tangy sauce (originally from England) that adds savory depth to beef dishes without any strong flavor of its own.
